title: Adding Ebola to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate reported version is repeated here.)

Adding Ebola to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act - (Sec. 2) Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to add filoviruses, a family of viruses that includes the Ebola virus, to the list of tropical diseases under the priority review voucher program, which awards vouchers to sponsors of human drug applications that are approved to prevent or treat tropical diseases. (A voucher entitles the holder to have a future human drug application acted upon by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) within six months.)

Changes the process by which infectious diseases that do not significantly impact developed nations and disproportionately affect poor and marginalized populations can be designated as tropical diseases from rulemaking to order of the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS).

Allows priority review vouchers to be transferred between sponsors of human drug applications any number of times.

Reduces from 365 days to 90 days the advance notice required before submitting a human drug application subject to a priority review voucher.

summary.headline: This law adds Ebola-related viruses to the list of tropical diseases that can earn FDA priority review vouchers for drug makers.
summary.what_it_does: The law adds filoviruses, a virus family that includes Ebola, to the FDA's list of tropical diseases covered by the priority review voucher program. A voucher lets its holder have a future drug application reviewed by the FDA within six months. The law also lets HHS add diseases to the tropical list by order instead of through a formal rulemaking process. It allows vouchers to be sold or transferred between companies any number of times, and it cuts from 365 days to 90 days the advance notice required before submitting a drug application that uses a voucher.

who_it_affects.group: Drug companies developing treatments for Ebola or other filoviruses
who_it_affects.how: They can become eligible to receive priority review vouchers for approved Ebola-related drugs, which can speed FDA review of a later drug application.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that hold or buy priority review vouchers
who_it_affects.how: They can transfer vouchers to other sponsors as many times as needed, and they need only give 90 days' notice instead of 365 days before using one.
It can designate new tropical diseases by order rather than by going through a rulemaking process.

who_it_affects.group: People at risk from Ebola and related viruses
who_it_affects.how: The law is intended to encourage development of drugs to prevent or treat these infections, though it does not itself guarantee any new treatment.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 16, 2014; the summary does not specify separate effective dates for each provision.
